sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup, imports and output encoding
sections.what: Describes how to run the tool, imports the search and design system code, and makes the terminal output use UTF-8 so symbols print correctly on Windows. It also sets a 300 character cut-off for long text.
sections.why: The encoding fix is there because Windows terminals often default to a narrower character set that cannot print emoji.
sections.watch_out: The encoding change runs as soon as this file loads, so any other script that imports it also gets the changed output.

sections.name: format_output
sections.title: Turns search results into readable text
sections.what: Formats a search result as a readable list with headings and bold field names. When nothing matches, it says so and suggests retrying with other words before falling back to general defaults.
sections.why: Output is kept short so an AI helper does not spend too many tokens on long text.
sections.watch_out: Long values are cut at 300 characters unless the full option is used, so the answer you need may be hidden.

sections.name: entry point (part 1)
sections.title: Reads command options and builds a design system
sections.what: Reads all the command options and checks that the dial numbers fall between 1 and 10. If the design system option is set, it builds the design system and prints it, or prints JSON with the design system and save details.
sections.why: The design system path is checked first so it takes priority over stack and domain searches.
sections.watch_out: With the JSON option, the printed output includes only the design system and save details, not the text version.

sections.name: entry point (part 2)
sections.title: Save messages and regular searches
sections.what: In text mode with the save option, prints where the design system was saved, lists the created files, or warns that the master file already exists. If no design system was requested, it runs a stack search when a stack is given, or a domain search otherwise, and prints the result.
sections.why: The save messages tell the user where files went and how to use the page override files.
sections.watch_out: The save message only appears in text mode, so with the JSON option a saved file produces no message on screen.

summary: Command-line tool that searches the design guidance data or builds a full design system, then prints the result as text or JSON.
purpose: Lets a person or an AI helper look up design advice from the terminal, and optionally save a design system for a project.
why: Reason not stated in the code. It appears to be the main entry point that routes requests to the search and design system code.
how: Set up the output encoding for Windows. Read the command arguments. If the design system option is set, build it, print it, and optionally save it. Otherwise, if a stack is given, search that stack's guidance. Otherwise, search the chosen domain. Print the result as text or JSON.
inputs: A search phrase, plus optional settings: domain, stack, number of results, JSON output, full output, design system mode, project name, output format, save option, page name, output folder, force overwrite, and three 1 to 10 design dials.
outputs: Text or JSON printed to the terminal. When saving, design files are written under a design-system folder.
risks: Saving writes files into the output folder. If that option is left out, the current working folder is used. Text output cuts long values unless the full option is set.
debug: If results are empty, check the spelling of the domain or stack, try broader words, and confirm the data files exist. If a save does nothing, check whether the master file already exists and whether force is needed. If Windows output looks garbled, check the encoding setup at the top of the file.
